test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a revenue expenditure?

options.text: Expenses incurred as lawyer's fee to defend a suit claiming that the firm's factory site belonged to the Plaintiff. The suit was not successful.
Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a licensee for starting a factory.
Expenses incurred for removal of stock to a new site.
Expenses incurred to change rings and pistons of an engine to get full efficiency.

solution:
The correct answer is** Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a license for starting a factory.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a license for starting a factory:**

 
 
• This is considered a capital expenditure because it is a one-time cost associated with setting up the business and acquiring a long-term asset. It provides benefits over a long period and is not a recurring expense.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Expenses incurred as lawyer's fee to defend a suit claiming that the firm's factory site belonged to the Plaintiff. The suit was not successful:**

 
 
• This is a revenue expenditure as it is a recurring cost associated with the normal operations of the business. It does not result in the acquisition of a long-term asset.
 
 
 
• **Expenses incurred for removal of stock to a new site:**
 
 
• This is also a revenue expenditure. It is a cost associated with the day-to-day operations of the business and does not provide long-term benefits.
 
 
 
• **Expenses incurred to change rings and pistons of an engine to get full efficiency:**
 
 
• This is considered a revenue expenditure as it is a maintenance cost aimed at ensuring the asset (engine) continues to operate efficiently. It does not extend the life of the asset but maintains its current operational capacity.
